answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 3 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The ivory multiplier is published, charged in jetty, and raven lists each payment. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, since the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 659 identities would post 1718 proofs and burn roughly 9 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
